@@identicalOkWhy: Keys that may legitimately come back byte-identical to English — a brand name, an email address, or a word many languages borrow unchanged. Everything NOT listed here and identical to English is treated as untranslated and fails the build. Keep this list short: it is an exemption from the check that catches the most common translation failure.

meta.title: Daili — Family Organizer: Shared Calendar, Lists & To-Dos

@title.description: Browser tab and search result title.

meta.description: Daili is the simple way to run family life together: one shared calendar, live shopping lists and family to-dos — on iPhone, Android and the web.
meta.ogDescription: One calm place for your family's week: shared calendar, shopping lists and to-dos everyone can see — on every phone and in the browser.
meta.supportDescription: Get help with Daili, or delete your account. We usually answer within a day or two.

@help.description: Footer link to the help center (daili.app/help/, English only). Shown once the help center is public. One short word, like the Blog link.

@menu.description: aria-label on the burger button that opens the mobile navigation. Never shown as visible text.

store.iosSoon: Daili is coming to the App Store very soon.

@h1b.description: Highlighted in forest green with a hand-drawn underline beneath it. Keep it short — this is the emphasised half of the headline.

@notes.description: Three short trust chips under the download buttons. Two or three words each.

@home.description: Every string of the new home page (bevel layout, 2026-09-28). Person names (Lena, Marco, Emma, Noah, Mia, Oma Rosi, Opa Karl) and product names (iPhone, Android, Apple Watch, TRMNL, Google Calendar, Outlook, YouTube, Google Gemini) stay exactly as written. "Daili", "Daili Plus" and "Minzi" are never translated. Times are 24-hour; weekdays and dates use the locale's normal short style.

@nav.description: Top navigation of the home page: four section links, the web-app login link and the pill button. One or two words each.

@qr.description: Floating QR card at the bottom corner on desktop. t = bold title (≤ 20 chars, keeps "daili"), s = one short line, alt = the QR image's alt text.

qr.s: Scan with your phone camera. iPhone & Android.

@hero.description: Hero under the headline (the headline itself reuses hero.h1a/h1b). lead = the paragraph under it (≤ 170 chars), cta = the dark download button, alt = the phone + watch image.

hero.lead: One calm place for your family's week: calendar, lists, to-dos, habits and notes that everyone can see. On every phone, on your wrist, and in the browser.
hero.alt: The Daili home screen on a phone, with an Apple Watch showing the next event

@cards.description: 7 small cards floating around the hero phone, top-left first. They imitate app content. t ≤ 20 chars (bold line), s ≤ 26 chars (small grey line). Names stay as written.

@watch.description: Tiny texts on the drawn Apple Watch face next to the hero phone (~60 px wide). Keep them as short as the English.

@works.description: Scrolling "works with" strip under the hero. label = the small caption. items = short labels, no full stop; product names stay in Latin letters, only "Home-screen widgets" and "Web browser" are translated.

@badges.description: Two badges above the members headline. t = bold (≤ 16 chars), s = small line (≤ 24 chars). "From Deutsch to Türkçe" keeps the two language names as endonyms.

@h2a.description: First line of the members headline. {count} is filled by the build with the locale-formatted member number (1,000 / 1.000) and must appear exactly once.

@cards.description: 8 photo cards in the members carousel. cap = a short, casual, handwritten-style caption on the photo (≤ 28 chars) — write it the way a parent would caption their own photo in your language, not a translation of the English joke; "Day 12. Minzi is proud." keeps Minzi. t/s = the Daili widget drawn on the photo (t ≤ 24, s ≤ 30). "Oma" and "Papa" may become your language's word for grandma / dad here only.

@tiles.description: Two tiles at the end of the members carousel. First: big = the price ("€0" written the locale's way), t = one line. Second: t = one line next to Minzi the cat.

tiles.t: No ads, no trial, no catch.
Minzi, the family cat, cheers you on

@day.description: "Start the day together" section: headline, sub line (≤ 80 chars) and three feature cards. h3 = the feature name (use the app's word), p = two short sentences, t/s = the small app widget on the card (t ≤ 24, s ≤ 32).

day.sub: Everything your family needs to know, in the places you already look.

cards.p: Everyone's week at a glance. School, swimming and the dentist, each person in their own colour.
Add milk in the kitchen, tick it off in the shop. Everyone sees it straight away.
Small routines, done together. Every tick gives Minzi, your family cat, more energy.
cards.s: 6 more and Minzi goes on a trip

@dinner.description: Meal-plan card. chips = three short labels, no full stop. t/s = the recipe widget, add = its button (use the locale's name of the shopping list).

dinner.p: Plan the week's meals, keep the family recipes, and send the ingredients to your shopping list in one tap.

@calendars.description: Calendar-sync card. t/s = the connected-calendar widget (Google Calendar stays as written).

calendars.p: Bring in Google, Outlook and your phone's calendar. Add public holidays for your country. See it all next to the family plan.

@plus.description: Daili Plus section (dark). "Daili Plus" and "Daili Intelligence" are product names and stay in Latin letters. Each card: h3 + p, then a drawn widget: hd = its small header, title/t/s = its lines, add = its button (all ≤ 28 chars).

plus.sub: Smart helpers that turn videos, photos and ideas into plans, so you can get back to your family.

video.p: Paste a YouTube link. Daili writes down the ingredients and the steps for you.
video.title: Crispy chickpea curry

letter.h3: Snap a letter, get the dates
letter.p: Take a photo of the school letter. Daili finds the dates and adds them to your calendar.

@rows.description: Three events found in the school letter. s = the date in the locale's short style, 24-hour time.

ideas.p: Out of ideas? Get dinner suggestions for the whole week, then add the ones you like to your meal plan.
ideas.title: Veggie lasagne
ideas.s: Tap to add it to Thursday

plus.fine: Daili Plus features use Google Gemini, and only when you use them.

@flow.description: "See it in action": four steps (t = title, d = one or two sentences) and, in the same order, four toast notifications on the drawn phone (t ≤ 24, s ≤ 26). pill = the tiny event pill on the drawn calendar (≤ 12 chars).

flow.sub: Four everyday moments, start to finish.

items.d: Add swimming for Noah on Tuesday. It shows up on every phone in the family, in his colour.
Marco is at the store and ticks off the milk. At home you see it right away, no double buying.
Noah finishes the laundry and ticks it. The whole family sees what is still open.
Stretch for five minutes, tick it, and watch Minzi get more energy for her next trip.

@screens.description: "On every screen" section: five cards (h3 + p). widgets.* and trmnl.days are tiny texts inside drawn screens (~60–120 px) — keep them as short as the English. widgets.items = three grocery items, no full stop. trmnl.days = four short weekday names with their events.

screens.h2: On every screen in your home
screens.sub: Glance at your wrist, your home screen or the kitchen wall. The same family plan, everywhere.

watch.p: What's next, and the shopping list, right on your wrist.

widgets.p: Next up, shopping, to-dos, habits, notes and birthdays on your home screen.

trmnl.p: Show the family week on a TRMNL e-paper screen in the hallway. No glow, no noise.

web.p: Plan the week on a big screen at app.daili.app. The same family, the same plans.
web.alt: The Daili web app showing a family calendar

@phones.description: phones.p: the two example languages may change to fit your locale (for tr: grandma speaks German, the kids speak Turkish). Keep the idea: two generations, two languages, one app. Name languages by their endonym.

phones.p: iPhone and Android, in 25 languages. Grandma speaks Türkçe, the kids speak English? No problem.

@privacy.description: Privacy section. chips = six short labels, no full stop ("EU" may be the locale's usual abbreviation).

privacy.sub: Your family's plans belong to your family. That is not a setting, it is how Daili is built.
chips: Documents & photos stay on your phone
AI only when you use it

@care.description: Two-line headline (h2b is the highlighted half) and one sentence under it.

care.sub: Designed and built in Tirol, Austria, for the everyday chaos of busy families.

@final.description: Last call-to-action section above the FAQ/footer: headline and one line.

final.sub: Start with one list. Add the calendar when you're ready. Daili grows with your family.

items.a: Nothing. Daili is free — no ads, no data selling. If we ever add paid extras, everything that is free today stays free.

Yes. Open app.daili.app in any browser on your computer and sign in with the same account. Calendar, lists, meals, birthdays and family are all there; photos and documents stay on your phone. The web app is in English and German.

The app speaks 19 languages, fully — including the reminders it sends: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, Polish, Czech, Slovak, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Turkish, Romanian, Bulgarian, Greek and Ukrainian.

items.q: Which phones does it run on?
items.a: iPhone and Android, from one shared family account. Everything syncs between them — and with the web app.

Yes — that's the point. Kids and teens get their own login and see their own tasks and events. Little ones without an email address get a managed profile a parent controls, which can be upgraded to a real login later. Parents are admins and can remove a profile and its data at any time.
You can read your calendar, lists and to-dos without a connection, and changes sync as soon as you're back online. Photos and documents in the vault are always offline — they live only on your phone.

items.q: Can I bring my existing calendar?
items.a: Daili can show your phone's own calendar next to the family calendar, on your device. Connecting a Google or Outlook calendar is coming soon.
Your calendar, lists and family data live on our server in the EU. Photos and documents in the vault never leave your phone. Details in the privacy policy.

support.intro: We're a small team and we read everything. Write to support@daili.app — questions, problems or ideas.
support.helpsIntro: If something isn't working, it helps us a lot if you include:
helps: Your phone model and whether it's iPhone or Android
What you did, what you expected, and what happened instead
A screenshot, if you have one
support.replyTime: We usually answer within a day or two.
support.deleteIntro: You can delete your Daili account and its data at any time, in two ways:
deleteWays: In the app: Settings → Profile → Delete account.
By email: write to support@daili.app from the email address of your account, with the subject “Delete my account”.
support.deleteWhat: What happens next: your account is deactivated immediately and you receive an email with a cancellation link. After a 30-day grace period, your account and the data linked to it (profile, and any events, lists, recipes and photos you created) are permanently deleted from our servers. If you change your mind within those 30 days, the link in the email restores everything. Files in the offline vault live only on your phone and are removed when the account is deleted on that device.
